questions.question: Earth’s core is mainly made up of ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**nickel and iron**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Core:

__
 
• The innermost layer is the core with a radius of about 3500 km.
 
• The central core has a very high temperature and pressure.
 
• The inner core (1200 km) is in the solid state whereas the outer core (2300 km) is in the liquid state.
 
• The innermost layer is the core with a radius of about 3500 km and divided into Inner and Outer core.
 
• The inner core is with a radius of 350 km mainly made up of- nickel and iron. The innermost layer is also called ‘nife’ (ni - nickel and fe - ferrous- iron).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

The Earth is divided into four main layers: the solid crust on the outside, the mantle, the outer core, and the inner core.

 
• All those layers are separated from each other through a transition zone.
 
• These transition zones are called discontinuities.
 
 
• Conrad Discontinuity: It lies between the Upper crust and Lower crust.
 
• Mohorovicic Discontinuity: It lies between crust and mantle.
 
• Repiti Discontinuity: It lies between the Upper mantle and Lower mantle.
 
• Gutenberg Discontinuity: It lies between core and mantle.
 
• Lehman Discontinuity: It lies between the upper core and lower core.
 
 

 

Interior of the Earth:

Crust:

 
• The uppermost layer over the earth’s surface is called the crust.
 
• It is the thinnest of all the layers.
 
• on the continental masses, It is about 35 km and on the ocean floors, only 5 km.
 
• The crust is the thinnest layer of the Earth and it amounts to less than 1% of our planet's volume.
 
• The earth is made up of several concentric layers with one inside another, just like an onion.
 
• The crust is the outermost layer of Earth and is made up of igneous, metamorphic, and sedimentary rocks. 
 
• The Earth's crust is unstable because of the exogenic forces.

Mantle:

 
• The Mantle extends up to a depth of 2900 km below the crust.
 
• It is the widest section of the Earth.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/48efa67620a436865d28875e1ad3ed6258e900c7490222023ce2a3aa42503d71.png] [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d57857c9be9454cf6f6786933ab6ff36087ae2b0dfa406e02f67ffd7925c1b50.png]

questions.question: The subject of the Study of Macro Economics is based on which principle?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The principle of National Income.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Principle of National Income:**

 
 
• The value of the **commodities and services** a nation produces in a fiscal year is referred to as national income.
 
• As a result, it represents the **sum of all economic activity **carried out in a nation over the course of a year.
 
• It is valued in **monetary terms.**
 
• The terms "national income" and "national dividend," as well as "national output" and "national spending," are** ambiguous.**
 
 
 
• **Macro Economics:**
 
 
• It is the study o**f how economies function,** including changes in the **balance of payments, inflation, interest and foreign exchange rates,** and **economic production.**
 
• Only with **solid monetary and fiscal policy** are poverty alleviation, social equality, and sustainable growth conceivable.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Consumer theory:**

 
 
• **Microeconomics** includes the field of consumer theory.
 
• It investigates how people choose **what to buy** with their money based on their tastes and financial restrictions.
 
 
 
• **Producer theory:**
 
 
• The producers theory looks at how businesses recruit and combine **productive inputs to produce goods** at reasonable rates.

questions.question: The Durga temple at Aihole, built about ______ years ago.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** 1400**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Aihole, Karnataka, India **is home to the **early eighth-century** Hindu temple known as the Durga temple.
 
• It was originally **dedicated to Surya.**
 
• Its relief panels, which feature the artwork of** Shaivism, Vaishnavism, Shaktism, and Vedic deities**, are the largest and most elaborate in Aihole.
 
• It is renowned for its** apsidal layout, **a unique example of early **Chalukyan Hindu temple construction.**
 
• It is part of a** pending UNESCO **World Heritage Site application.

 [IMAGE: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9d/Durga_Temple_-_General_View.jpg/800px-Durga_Temple_-_General_View.jpg] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Aihole

 
 
• It was built in **634**.
 
• It was the headquarters of the famous medieval Ayyavole merchants’ guild and was an important commercial centre.
 
• The earliest stone-built temple is Lad Khan temple.
 
• A temple dedicated to the goddess Durga was built on the model of Buddha, Chaitya.
 
• It stands on a raised platform in the form of a semi-circle.
 
 
 
• Badami
 
 
• There are four caves in Badami.
 
• The largest cave temple built by Mangalesa is dedicated to Vishnu.
 
• The reclining posture of Vishnu on the snake bed and Narasimha are exquisite examples of Chalukya art.
 
 
 
• Pattadakal
 
 
• It is a village in the Bagalkot district of Karnataka.
 
• It is famous for its exquisite temples.
 
• Pattadakal was a centre for performing royal rituals.
 
• The Virupaksha temple was built at the order of queen Lohamahadevi to commemorate the conquest of Kanchipuram by her husband Vikramaditya II.

questions.question: According to the Brihat Samhita, what do you call the process of making scents, mouth perfumes and bath powders?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gandhayukli.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• An** encyclopaedia **written in Sanskrit and published in the** sixth century in Ujjain** was called **Brhat-Samhita.**
 
• In addition to divination, the book covers a wide range of topics, such as** astronomy, planetary motion, eclipses, rainfall, architecture, crop development, perfume production, matrimony, household relationships, gems, and ceremonies.**
 
• **Varahmihir’s Brihat Samhita **gives references to perfumes and cosmetics.
 
• Recipes for hair dying were made from plants, like indigo and minerals like iron power, black iron or steel and acidic extracts of sour rice gruel.
 
• **Gandhayukli describes recipes for making scents, mouth perfumes, bath powders, incense and talcum powder.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kamplcica, Pattanga and Jatuka:**

 
 
• **A number of classical texts, like Atharvaveda (1000 BCE) **mention some **dye stuff, the material used were turmeric, madder, sunflower, orpiment, cochineal and lac.**
 
• Some other substances having tinting properties were **Kamplcica, Pattaya and Jatuka.**

questions.question: Which organic compound has the structure R−COOH, with R referring to the alkyl, alkenyl, aryl, or other group?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Carboxylic acid**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• ​A** carboxyl group (C(=O)OH)** coupled to an **R-group** makes up a carboxylic acid, an **organic acid.**
 
• The general formula of a** carboxylic acid is R−COOH or R−CO2H**, with R referring to the **alkyl, alkenyl, aryl, or other group.**
 
• **Carboxylic acids** are very common.
 
• The** amino acids and fatty acids** are two prime examples.
 
• A** carboxylate anion** is produced when a carboxylic acid is** deprotonated.**
 
• They produce **carboxylate ions** when they interact with** metals and alkalis.**
 
• The reactions of carboxylic acids show how **acidic **they are.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ester:**

 
 
• An ester is a substance that is formed from an** acid in which an organyl grou**p has been substituted for at least one of the** acid's acidic hydrogen atoms.**
 
• Different esters are used in the creation of **pheromones, essential oils, and fragrances.**
 
 
 
• **Ketone**:
 
 
• A ketone is a functional group that has the** formula R-C-R', where R and R' **can be any number of substituents that include carbon.
 
• Ketones have a** carbonyl group, or C**, in them.
 
• **Acetone** is the most basic ketone.
 
 
 
• **Aldehydes:**
 
 
• ​An organic molecule with the **functional group RCH=O i**s known as an aldehyde. 
 
• Natural aldehydes can be found in** nuts, spices, fruits, and vegetables.**

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India authorises the President to seek the opinion of the Supreme Court in specific categories of matters?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Article 143__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Article 143: Power of President to consult Supreme Court.

 
 
• If at any time it appears to the President that a question of law or fact has arisen, or is likely to arise, which is of such a nature and such public importance that it is expedient to obtain the opinion of the Supreme Court upon it, he may refer the question to that Court for consideration and the Court may, after such hearing as it thinks fit, report to the President its opinion thereon.
 
• The President may, notwithstanding anything in the proviso to article 131, refer a dispute of the kind mentioned in the said proviso to the Supreme Court for opinion and the Supreme Court shall, after such hearing as it thinks fit, report to the President its opinion thereon.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Article 142 of the Constitution:
 
• Title: Enforcement of decrees, orders of Supreme Court and orders as to discovery, etc.
 
• Provisions: This article has 2 provisions –
 
 
• 142(1): The Supreme Court may pass an order for doing complete justice. *Hence, option 2 is correct.*
 
• 142(2): It confers three different powers on the Supreme Court. 
 
 
 
• Article 144
 
 
• The Indian Constitution's Article 144 instructs civil and judicial agencies to support the Supreme Court in its work. It states that the Supreme Court shall get assistance from all civil and judicial bodies within the boundaries of India. Additional Reading: Indian Supreme Court.
 
 
 
• Article 145
 
 
• Rules of Court
 
• Subject to the provisions of any law made by Parliament the Supreme Court may from time to time, with the approval of the President, make rules for regulating generally the practise and procedure of the Court.

questions.question: The ‘flag-raising’ ceremony by the Prime Minister of India on Independence Day is held at which of the following places in Delhi?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Red Fort**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• On 15 August 1947, the** first Prime Minister of India, Jawaharlal Nehru** r**aised the Indian national flag above the Lahori Gate of the Red Fort in Delhi.**
 
• From August 15, 1947, to 1964, he unfurled the Indian flag at Red Fort for continuous 17 years.​
 
• Every year, the Prime Minister of India unfurls the flag at the Red Fort, but there are some who got a chance to become PM of India but were not able to hoist the flag at the iconic monument.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• List of Prime Ministers who hoisted the flag at Red Fort more than five times:

 
 
• Indira Gandhi - From 1966 to 1977, she got the opportunity for nothing less than 11 times.
 
• Manmohan Singh - Ex-Prime Minister of India unfurled the flag 10 times. 
 
• Narendra Modi - Current Prime Minister of India, Narendra Modi has been hoisting the Indian flag at the Red fort since 2014 till date.
 
• Atal Bihari Vajpayee - He is the only non-Congress Prime Minister who has unfurled the Indian Flag at Red Fort six times.
 
• Rajiv Gandhi and Narasimha Rao unfurled the Indian flag five times each.

questions.question: The British Parliament transferred the powers of the East India company to the British crown in ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1858.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• On **August 2, 1858,** a measure to **transfer control of India** from the **East Indian Company** to the British Crown was approved by** Parliament.**
 
• For the** highest-ranking representative **of the British Government in India, the **title of viceroy** was established.
 
• This bill's clause asked for the **British East India Company**, which ruled India with the** support of the Parliament,** to be dissolved and its authority to be transferred to the British Crown.
 
• This law was introduced by **Lord Palmerston, the UK's prime minister **at the time.
 
• To quell the repercussions of the revolt, this** legislation was passed in 1858,** the year after India's first war of independence.
 
• Right till the** nineteenth century **nothing threatened the rule of the British in the** Indian sub-continent,** until the first Indian war of Independence in **1857. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• East india company was incorporated in **England in 1600** and eventually becoming **British.**
 
• **East India Company **was disbanded in **1874.**
 
• It was established to engage in trade with the **East Indies and later, East Asia, in the Indian Ocean region.**
 
• The British East India Company first arrived in India as a **spice dealer.**
 
• Other from that, their main commodities were **opium, silk, cotton, indigo dye, and tea.**
 
• On **August 24, 1608, **they arrived in the Indian subcontinent at the **port of Surat.**

questions.question: According to census 2001, sex ratio is ______ females per 1000 males.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**933.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to census 2001, sex ratio is **933 females per 1000 males.**
 
• The sex ratio is used to describe the **number of females per 1000 males.**
 
• Sex ratio is a valuable source for finding the population of women in India and what is the ratio of women to that men in India.
 
• In the **Population Census of 2011**, it was revealed that the population ratio in India in 2011 is 943, little higher than 2001.
 
• The Sex Ratio 2011 shows an upward trend from the census 2001 data.
 
• Census 2001 revealed that there were** 933 females to that 1000 males.**
 
• For decades India has seen a decrease in the sex ratio in 2011, but in the last two decades, there has been a slight increase in the sex ratio.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Census 2011**

 
 
• The Indian Census is the most credible source of information on Demography (Population characteristics), Economic Activity, Literacy and Education, Housing Household Amenities, Urbanization, Fertility and Mortality, etc. 
 
• Census 2011 was the **15th National Census of the Country.**
 
• Census was introduced in India during the era of Lord Mayo in the year **1872**.
 
• It came into force in **1881**.
 
• This census was conducted under the guidance of Mr. **C. Chandramouli**.
 
• The slogan of census 2011 was ‘**Our Census, Our future**’.

questions.question: The Central Universities (Amendment) Bill, 2022 was passed in Lok Sabha in ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**August**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Central Universities (Amendment) Bill, 2022 was passed in Lok Sabha in **August**.
 
• The Central Universities (Amendment) Bill, 2022 was introduced in Lok Sabha on** August 1, 2022. **
 
• **The Bill amends the Central Universities Act, 2009, **which provides for establishing central universities in various states. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Key features of the Bill include:**
 
• **Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya: **
 
 
• The Bill seeks to convert the National Rail and Transportation Institute, Vadodara (a deemed university) to the Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya, which will be a central university. 
 
 
 
• **Scope of education:**
 
 
• The Bill provides that Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya will take measures to provide quality teaching, research, and skill development in disciplines related to transportation, technology, and management. 
 
 
 
• **Appointment of a new Vice-Chancellor (VC):**
 
 
• The existing VC of the National Rail and Transportation Institute will hold office for: (i) six months from when the Act is notified, or (ii) until a new VC for the Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya is appointed, whichever is earlier.

questions.question: Which of the following is used in photography?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sodium thiosulphate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Sodium thiosulfate 

 
 
• Sodium thiosulfate (sodium hyposulfite), Na2S2O3, is used by photographers to fix developed negatives and prints.
 
• It acts by dissolving the part of the silver salts coated onto film which remains unchanged by exposure to light.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sodium bicarbonate**

 
 
• Baking Soda is the common name for Sodium Bicarbonate.
 
• Its chemical formula is NaHCO__3.
 
• It is a crystalline white solid that is salty and alkaline.
 
• It is used for cooking purpose, pest control, and as a fire extinguisher. 
 
 

 
• Sodium hydroxide

 
 
• Sodium hydroxide (NaOH) is known as 'caustic soda' and it is a 'high-base' alkali.
 
• It is used in the manufacture of pulp and paper cloth, drinking water, soap, and detergent.
 
• In the field of medicine, sodium hydroxide is used for the treatment, control, prevention, and improvement of diseases.
 
• Sodium benzoate is used as a preservative for carbonated drinks, jams and fruit juices, and pickles.
 
 

 
• ​Sodium sulfate

 
 
• The formula for sodium is – Na+, and Sulphate is – SO42-. So, the formula for Sodium Sulphate is – Na2SO4.
 
• Sodium sulfate is used to dry organic liquids.
 
• As a filler in powdered home laundry detergents. 
 
• **Na2SO4 **is used in manufactured paper, glass, dyes, and pharmaceuticals.
 
• It is often used in its decahydrate form, which is also known as Glauber's salt.
 
• It is also called **salt cake**.

questions.question: Who among the following rulers appointed Ladha and Pira, two gardeners to high administrative post?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Muhammad Tughluq.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Muhammad Tughluq **appointed Ladha and Pira, two gardeners to high administrative posts.
 
• Sultan Muhammad Tughluq appointed:
 
 
• Aziz Khummar, a wine distiller,
 
• Firuz Hajjam, a barber,
 
• Manka Tabbakh, a cook, and
 
• Two gardeners, Ladha and Pira, to high administrative posts.
 
 
 
• **Ziyauddin Barani,** a mid-fourteenth-century chronicler, reported their appointments as a sign of Sultan’s loss of political judgment and his incapacity to rule.
 
• **Barani **had criticized Muhammad Tughluq for that appointment.
 
• **Tughluq's** appointment reflected the socio-economic stereotypes that may have been prevalent in those times.
 
• The authors of **Persian tawarikh **criticized the Delhi Sultans for appointing the “low and base-born” to high offices.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Khizr Khan** was the founder of the Sayyid dynasty of the **Delhi Sultanate**.

 
 
• In 1414 AD, Khizr Khan occupied the power of Delhi.
 
• He did not hold the title of Sultan and declared himself as **‘Rayat-e-Ala’.**
 
• He was the founder of the Sayyid Dynasty in India and ruled as a deputy of Timur’s son and successor, Shah Rukh.
 
• His reign was marked by utter chaos and disorder.
 
 
 
• The Lodi dynasty was founded by** Bahlul Khan Lodi**.
 
 
• The Lodi dynasty was an Afghan dynasty.
 
• The Lodi dynasty was the last dynasty in Delhi Sultanate, ruled from 1451 to 1526.
 
 
 
• ​Iltutmish was a king of the Slave dynasty.
 
 
• He became a ruler of the Slave dynasty from 1211 to 1236.
 
• He made Delhi the capital of his kingdom by replacing Lahore.
 
• He introduced the silver coin(Tanka) and the copper coin(Jital).
 
• He completed the construction of the Qutb Minar.

questions.question: To safeguard public property and to abjure violence is a ________ in the Indian Constitution.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is fundamental duty.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• List of fundamental duties -
 
 
• Abide by the Constitution and respect the national flag & National Anthem
 
• Follow the ideals of the freedom struggle
 
• Protect the sovereignty & integrity of India
 
• Defend the country and render national services when called upon
 
• Spirit of common brotherhood
 
• Preserve composite culture
 
• Preserve natural environment 
 
• Develop scientific temper
 
• Safeguard public property and abjure violence
 
• Strive for excellence
 
• Duty for all parents/guardians to send their children in the age group of 6-14 years to school.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Fundamental Duties:
 
 
• Article 51-A, Part IV-A of the Indian Constitution deals with Fundamental Duties.
 
• This article was added to the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee.
 
• Fundamental Duties are Non-justiciable in nature.
 
• Fundamental Duties in the Indian constitution are inspired by the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR.
 
• These are confined to Indian citizens only and do not extend to foreigners.
 
• These are enforceable, which means the parliament is free to enforce them by suitable legislation.
 
• As of today, there are 11 fundamental duties included in Article 51-A.

questions.question: _________ measures the aggregate production of final goods and services taking place within the domestic economy during a year.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gross domestic product**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****Gross domestic product (GDP)**

__
 
• It is the standard monetary measure of the value-added created through the **production of goods and services **in a country during a certain period
 
• As such, it also measures the income earned from that production or the** total amount **spent on final goods and services (fewer imports)
 
• As a broad measure of overall domestic production, its functions as a comprehensive scorecard of a given country's economic performance.
 
• In India, the GDP is released by the **National Statistical Office (NSO)**. Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation on a quarterly and yearly basis.
 
• The formula to calculate GDP is of t**hree types: Expenditure Approach, Income Approach, and Production Approach**.
 
• **Expenditure Approach**
 
 
• GDP = Consumption + Investment + Government Spending + Net Export
 
 
 
• **Income Approach**
 
 
• GDP = Total National Income + Sales Taxes + Depreciation + Net Foreign Factor Income
 
 
 
• **Production or Value-Added Approach**
 
 
• Gross Value Added = Gross Value of Output – Value of Intermediate Consumption
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gross national product (GNP) **is an estimate of the total value of all the final products and services turned out in a given period by the means of production owned by a country's residents. GNP is commonly calculated by taking the sum of personal consumption expenditures, private domestic investment, government expenditure, net exports, and any income earned by residents from overseas investments, then subtracting income earned by foreign residents. 
 
• **Net national product (NNP)** is the monetary value of finished goods and services produced by a country's citizens, overseas and domestically, in a given period. It is the equivalent of the gross national product (GNP), the total value of a nation's annual output, minus the amount of GNP required to purchase new goods to maintain existing stock.
 
• The **gross national product at factor cost** is the difference between the gross national product and net indirect taxes. It is also called gross national income. Gross national income is the total compensation of employees, operating surplus, mixed income, depreciation and net factor income from abroad.

questions.question: Nuts, vegetable oil, and fish are good source of which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Healthy fats**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Monounsaturated **fats and **polyunsaturated **fats are known as the “good fats” because they are good for your heart, your cholesterol, and your overall health.
 
• These fats can help to **lower the risk of heart disease** and stroke, cholesterol levels, and Prevent abnormal heart rhythms.
 
• Monounsaturated fat good sources include olive, canola, peanut, and sesame oils, Nuts (almonds, peanuts, macadamia, hazelnuts, pecans, cashews), avocados etc.
 
• Polyunsaturated fat good sources include Sunflower, sesame, and pumpkin seeds, Walnuts, Fatty fish (salmon, tuna, mackerel, herring, trout, sardines) fish oil, Soybean and safflower oil, etc.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Unhealthy fats **

 
 
• Trans fat. Small amounts of naturally occurring trans fats can be found in meat and dairy products but it's artificial trans fats that are considered dangerous. 
 
• This is the worst type of fat since it not only raises bad LDL cholesterol but also lowers good HDL levels.
 
 
 
• **Carbohydrates**
 
 
• They're the body's primary source of energy and the brain's preferred energy source. Carbs are broken down by the body into glucose.
 
 
 
• **Minerals**
 
 
• Minerals are those elements in foods that our bodies need to develop and function normally.
 
• Those essential for health include calcium, phosphorus, potassium, sodium, chloride, magnesium, iron, zinc, iodine, etc.
 
 
 
• **Protein**
 
 
• Protein is considered the building block of life and is found in every cell of the body.
 
• Protein is made up of amino acids that are attached to one another in long chains.
